Precalculus | Quarter 2 | Unit 3: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions

The Barometric Altimeter

How a bike computer knows your altitude

Duration
50 minutes
Grade level
Grades 11–12
Topic
Logarithmic Models
Standards
HSF-LE.A.4, HSF-BF.B.5, HSS-ID.B.6a

Students define logarithms as inverses of exponentials, build logarithmic models, linearise exponential data with logarithms, and use the pressure–altitude model inside a bike computer.

2Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson, students will be able to:

  • Convert between exponential and logarithmic form.
  • Build and evaluate logarithmic models.
  • Linearise exponential data by taking logarithms.
  • Use and interpret logarithmic scales.

3Essential question

If air pressure falls exponentially as you climb, how can a bike computer turn a pressure reading into an altitude?

5MTB connection

Most GPS bike computers and watches measure altitude with a barometer, because air pressure falls predictably as you climb. Pressure is exponential in altitude, so altitude is logarithmic in pressure.

Weather changes the sea-level pressure, which is why these devices drift and ask to be calibrated at a known elevation.

The mathOn the trail
Exponential decayAir pressure with altitude
LogarithmAltitude from pressure
CalibrationSetting the sea-level reference
LinearisingChecking pressure data fit the model
